inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL date-query reference combines WEEKDAY with calendar extraction functions such as YEAR, WEEKOFYEAR, YEARWEEK, and WEEK to classify date ranges and inspect component values.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored financial milestone calendar report. Fixed timestamps exercise DATE_FORMAT, MONTHNAME, QUARTER, DAYOFYEAR, and WEEKDAY across a leap day, quarter boundaries, year end, weekend classification, and NULL input; source queries, schema, dates, and reporting purpose are not copied.

fixture_notes: Rows cover New Year's Day, leap day, quarter starts, a summer milestone, year end, and a NULL timestamp so calendar extraction and missing-value classification remain observable.
determinism_notes: All milestone IDs and timestamps are fixed literals, and output is ordered by the unique milestone ID with no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections.
setup: CREATE TABLE financial_milestones (milestone_id INT PRIMARY KEY, milestone_at DATETIME NULL, milestone_kind VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT milestone_id, milestone_kind, DATE_FORMAT(milestone_at, '%Y-%m-%d') AS milestone_day, MONTHNAME(milestone_at) AS month_label, QUARTER(milestone_at) AS quarter_number, DAYOFYEAR(milestone_at) AS day_number, WEEKDAY(milestone_at) AS weekday_number, CASE WHEN milestone_at IS NULL THEN 'missing' WHEN WEEKDAY(milestone_at) IN (5, 6) THEN 'weekend' WHEN QUARTER(milestone_at) = 4 THEN 'year-end-weekday' ELSE 'weekday' END AS calendar_class FROM financial_milestones ORDER BY milestone_id
